message.content:
The famous scene where Del Boy falls through the bar is from the episode **"Yuppy Love"**, which was the first episode of **Series 6** of *Only Fools and Horses*. It originally aired on **8th January 1989** on BBC1.

In this iconic scene, Del Boy (played by Sir David Jason) and Trigger (played by Roger Lloyd Pack) are in a trendy wine bar trying to impress two women. Del tells Trigger to "play it nice and cool, son, nice and cool," but when he goes to lean on the bar, he doesn't realise the barman has lifted the counter hatch, and he falls straight through to the floor. Trigger then looks around wondering where Del has gone.

This scene has been voted the funniest sitcom moment in British television history on multiple occasions. Interestingly, the scene wasn't originally scripted exactly as it appeared - Sir David Jason insisted on falling all the way through rather than just stumbling, overruling writer John Sullivan's original idea. Additionally, Trigger wasn't originally meant to be in the scene; Roger Lloyd Pack apparently turned up unannounced on the filming day, and John Sullivan decided to include him, with Trigger's bemused reaction adding to the comedy.
